answer: In a poll on whether visitors may wander near a ferrous sculpture in the canyon, officials group ballots into batches of ten and randomly audit one ID per batch against a registry. They count a batch only if its sampled ID is valid and appears on no other submitted ballot; otherwise they discard the batch. Reusing an ID risks losing a batch, and obtaining other IDs may cost recruitment effort. Borrowed IDs can pass, and a failed audit discards genuine ballots.
